verses.text: Now, Israel, listen to the rules and laws I am teaching you. Obey them, so that you may live and go in and take over the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Do not add anything to what I command you, and do not take anything away from it. Just obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
You saw with your own eyes what the LORD did at Baal Peor. The LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed the god Baal of Peor.
But all of you who held on to the LORD your God are still alive today.
Look, I have taught you rules and laws, just as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you will obey them in the land you are going to take over.

Obey them carefully, for this will show the nations how wise and understanding you are. When they hear about all these rules, they will say, "This great nation really is a wise and understanding people!"
What other nation, however great, has a god as near to them as the LORD our God is to us whenever we pray to him?
And what other nation, however great, has rules and laws as fair as all this teaching I am giving you today?

But be careful, and watch yourselves closely, so that you do not forget the things you have seen with your own eyes. Do not let them slip from your heart as long as you live. Teach them to your children and to your grandchildren.

Remember the day you stood before the LORD your God at Mount Sinai, when he said to me, "Gather the people before me so they can hear my words. Then they will learn to fear me as long as they live on the earth, and they will teach these things to their children."
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. It was blazing with fire that reached up to the sky, and it was covered with darkness and thick black clouds.
Then the LORD spoke to you from the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you did not see any shape. There was only a voice.
He told you about his covenant, the Ten Commandments, which he commanded you to obey. He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you the rules and laws you must obey in the land you are going to take over.
On the day the LORD spoke to you at Mount Sinai from the fire, you did not see any shape. So be very careful,
and do not ruin yourselves by making an idol in any shape at all, whether in the form of a man or a woman,
or any animal on the land, or any bird that flies in the sky,
or any creature that crawls on the ground, or any fish in the water below the land.

And when you look up at the sky and see the sun, the moon, and the stars, all the lights of heaven, do not be tempted to bow down and worship them. The LORD your God has given them to all the nations under heaven.
But the LORD took you and brought you out of Egypt, out of that furnace for melting iron, to be his very own people, as you are today.
Because of you, the LORD was angry with me. He swore that I would not cross the Jordan and enter the good land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
I will die here in this land. I will not cross the Jordan, but you are about to cross over and take that good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant the LORD your God made with you. Do not make for yourselves an idol in any shape, which the LORD your God has forbidden.
For the LORD your God is a fire that burns everything up. He is a jealous God, who will not share your love with any other.

After you have had children and grandchildren and have lived in the land a long time, you may ruin yourselves by making an idol of any shape, doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God and making him angry.

If you do, I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will quickly disappear from the land you are crossing the Jordan to take. You will not live there long, but will be completely destroyed.
The LORD will scatter you among the nations, and only a few of you will survive among the nations where the LORD sends you.
There you will worship gods made by human hands, gods of wood and stone, which cannot see, hear, eat, or smell.
But if from there you look for the LORD your God, you will find him, if you look for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in trouble and all these things have happened to you, then in the days to come you will come back to the LORD your God and obey him.
For the LORD your God is a God full of mercy. He will not leave you or destroy you, and he will not forget the covenant he swore to your ancestors.

Ask about the days long ago, before your time, from the day God created human beings on the earth. Search from one end of heaven to the other. Has anything as great as this ever happened? Has anyone ever heard of anything like it?
Has any other people heard the voice of God speaking from a fire, as you have, and lived?

Has any god ever tried to take one nation out of another nation for himself, by testing, by miraculous signs and wonders, by war, by his mighty hand and powerful arm, and by great and terrifying acts? Yet that is what the LORD your God did for you in Egypt, right before your eyes.
He showed you these things so that you would know that the LORD is God. There is no other god besides him.
He let you hear his voice from heaven to teach you. On earth he let you see his great fire, and you heard his words from the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them. He himself brought you out of Egypt by his great power,
to drive out nations greater and stronger than you, and to bring you into their land and give it to you as your own, as it is today.
So know this today and keep it in your heart: the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other.

Obey his rules and commands that I am giving you today. Then all will go well with you and your children after you, and you will live a long time in the land the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three towns on the east side of the Jordan,
where someone who killed a person by accident, without having hated him before, could run for safety. He could run to one of these towns and save his life.
The towns were Bezer in the desert high plain for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the tribe of Manasseh.
This is the teaching Moses gave the people of Israel.
These are the instructions, rules, and laws Moses gave them after they came out of Egypt,

when they were east of the Jordan in the valley near Beth Peor. This was in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Moses and the people of Israel defeated him after they came out of Egypt.
They took over his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan, the two Amorite kings who ruled east of the Jordan.
This land went from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, to Mount Siyon, which is Mount Hermon,
and included the whole Jordan Valley east of the Jordan, as far as the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
